stem:
The structure of phenylethanoic acid is shown.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Give the number of different peaks in the carbon-13 ($^{13}\text{C}$) NMR spectrum of phenylethanoic acid.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Phenylethanoic acid, ethanol and phenol can all behave as acids.

Compare and explain the relative acidities of these three compounds.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem:
Phenylethanoic acid can be synthesised using benzene as the starting material.

In the first stage of this synthesis, benzene reacts with chloromethane in the presence of an $\text{AlCl}_3$ catalyst to form methylbenzene.

Chloromethane reacts with $\text{AlCl}_3$ to form two ions. One of these is the carbocation $^{+}\text{CH}_3$.
parts.text: Write an equation for the reaction between chloromethane and $\text{AlCl}_3$.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
Draw the mechanism of the reaction between benzene and $^{+}\text{CH}_3$. Include all relevant curly arrows, charges and the structure of the intermediate.

{{figure:pdf_visual_02.png}}

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.stem:
A three-step synthesis of phenylethanoic acid from methylbenzene is shown.

{{figure:pdf_visual_03.png}}
parts.text: State reagents and conditions for step 1.

parts.label: (d)(iii)
parts.text: State reagents and conditions for steps 2 and 3.

parts.label: (d)(iv)
parts.text: Draw the structure of an organic by-product that forms in step 1.
